source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: When the two Itô generator terms are time integrable. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Let $v$ be the vector with the given scalar drift rows and $\sigma_j$ the vector with the $j$th given noise column. Both generator terms displayed below are integrable in time for almost every sample.

The sample measure $\mu$ is finite. Time is nonnegative and the fixed horizon $T$ may equal zero. The coordinate set $I$ and noise index set $J$ are finite, with decidable equality on $I$. The filtration is indexed by nonnegative real time.
Each drift coordinate has integrable time sections for $\mu$-almost every sample. Each noise entry is a strongly progressive integrand with $L^2(\mu\otimes\ell_T)$ membership, where $\ell_T=\mathrm{Leb}|_{[0,T]}$.
The Euclidean path $X$ is almost surely continuous on $[0,T]$ and almost surely stays in the set $K$ at all horizon times. The ambient test $f$ is $C^2$ at each point of $K$.

Df(X_t)[v_t],\qquad \tfrac12\sum_{j\in J}D^2f(X_t)[\sigma_{j,t},\sigma_{j,t}]\quad\in L^1(\ell_T)\quad\text{a.s.}

lean.statement:
theorem anonymous_target.{u_1,
    u_2, u_3}
  {Ω : Type u_1} {I : Type u_2} {J : Type u_3} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J]
  {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : NNReal}
  (η :
    I → J → AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T)
  (b : I → NNReal → Ω → ℝ)
  (hbi :
    ∀ (i : I),
      ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun t => b i t ω)
          (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.TimeMeasure.upTo T))
  (X : NNReal → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ I) (hX : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => X t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T))
  {K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ I)} (hRange : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ∀ t ≤ T, X t ω ∈ K) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ)
  (hf : ∀ w ∈ K, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f w) :
  have v := fun t ω => WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => b i t ω;
  have σ := fun j t ω => WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => (η i j).process t ω;
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun t => (fderiv ℝ f (X t ω)) (v t ω))
        (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.TimeMeasure.upTo T) ∧
      MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun t => 1 / 2 * ∑ j, ((fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (X t ω)) (σ j t ω)) (σ j t ω))
        (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.TimeMeasure.upTo T)

blind_reconstruction.text:
Finite coordinate sets I and J; filtered finite measure space (Omega,m,mu,F); horizon T; integrands eta_ij; drift coordinates b_i; path X; set K; scalar f; v=(b_i), sigma_j=(eta_ij.process).

I,J are finite types; I has decidable equality. T is any nonnegative real. X:[0,infinity)×Omega→R^I, b_i:[0,infinity)×Omega→R, f:R^I→R, K⊆R^I. Time measure lambda_T is Lebesgue measure on [0,T], represented on nonnegative reals.

Assumptions: mu is finite. Each eta_ij is strongly progressive with (omega,t)↦eta_ij(t,omega) in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). For every i, b_i(·,omega) is lambda_T-integrable for mu-a.e. omega. X(·,omega) is continuous on [0,T] mu-a.e. and, on a mu-full set, X(t,omega)∈K for every t≤T. At every w∈K, f is C² at w in the ambient Euclidean space. There is no compactness assumption on K, no Brownian motion assumption, and no progressivity assumption on b or X.

Conclusion: For mu-a.e. omega, both t↦Df(X(t,omega))[v(t,omega)] and t↦(1/2)∑_{j∈J}D²f(X(t,omega))[sigma_j(t,omega),sigma_j(t,omega)] are integrable against lambda_T.

Quantifier order: Universally quantify all listed data. For each i assume pathwise drift integrability mu-a.e.; assume path continuity and all-time range inclusion mu-a.e. Conclusion has one mu-a.e. omega quantifier covering both integrability assertions.

Scope: Pathwise absolute integrability on the fixed horizon [0,T]; not integrability over Omega of these time integrals. T may be zero. No stochastic equation linking X, b and eta is assumed.

Constant dependencies: No existential numerical constants or rates.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.EuclideanBilinearCoordinates
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Comp
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoGeneratorIntegrability

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open ProgressiveL2
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.EuclideanBilinearCoordinates

private theorem integrable_continuousOn_mul
    {T : ℝ≥0} {W g : ℝ≥0 → ℝ}
    (hW : ContinuousOn W (Icc 0 T)) (hg : Integrable g (TimeMeasure.upTo T)) :
    Integrable (fun t => W t * g t) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
  let ν := TimeMeasure.upTo T
  have hMem : ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, t ∈ Icc 0 T :=
    (TimeMeasure.ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo T).mono fun _ ht => ⟨ht.1.le, ht.2⟩
  have hRest : ν.restrict (Icc 0 T) = ν := Measure.restrict_eq_self_of_ae_mem hMem
  have hm : AEStronglyMeasurable W ν := by
    rw [← hRest]
    exact hW.aestronglyMeasurable measurableSet_Icc
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := isCompact_Icc.bddAbove_image hW.norm
  exact hg.bdd_mul hm (hMem.mono fun t ht => hC ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩)

/-- Almost every continuous state path has integrable first- and second-order
Itô generator terms when the drift rows are pathwise integrable and the
progressive diffusion entries are square integrable in time and sample. -/
theorem ae_integrable_euclidean_generator_terms
    {Ω I J : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : ℝ≥0}
    (η : I → J → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T)
    (b : I → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ)
    (hbi : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Integrable (fun t => b i t ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T))
    (X : ℝ≥0 → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ I)
    (hX : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => X t ω) (Icc 0 T))
    {K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ I)}
    (hRange : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ t ≤ T, X t ω ∈ K)
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ) (hf : ∀ w ∈ K, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f w) :
    let v (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : I => b i t ω)
    let σ (j : J) (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) :=
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : I => (η i j).process t ω)
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ,
      Integrable (fun t => fderiv ℝ f (X t ω) (v t ω)) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) ∧
      Integrable (fun t => (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ∑ j : J,
        fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (X t ω) (σ j t ω) (σ j t ω)) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
  intro v σ
  have hProducts : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ i k : I, ∀ j : J,
      Integrable (fun t => (η i j).process t ω * (η k j).process t ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) :=
    ae_all_iff.2 fun i => ae_all_iff.2 fun k => ae_all_iff.2 fun j =>
      ((η i j).memLp.integrable_mul (η k j).memLp).prod_right_ae
  filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 hbi, hX, hRange, hProducts] with ω hDrift hPath hK hProduct
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ
  let D (t : ℝ≥0) := fderiv ℝ f (X t ω)
  let H (t : ℝ≥0) := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (X t ω)
  have hm : MapsTo (fun t => X t ω) (Icc 0 T) K := fun _ ht => hK _ ht.2
  have hD : ContinuousOn D (Icc 0 T) :=
    (show ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ f) K from fun w hw =>
      ((hf w hw).continuousAt_fderiv (by decide)).continuousWithinAt).comp hPath hm
  have hH : ContinuousOn H (Icc 0 T) :=
    (show ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f)) K from fun w hw =>
      (((hf w hw).fderiv_right (m := 1) (by decide)).continuousAt_fderiv
        (by decide)).continuousWithinAt).comp hPath hm
  constructor
  · have hi (i : I) : Integrable (fun t => D t (e i) * b i t ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) :=
      integrable_continuousOn_mul (hD.clm_apply continuousOn_const) (hDrift i)
    refine (integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hi i)).congr
      (Eventually.of_forall fun t => ?_)
    change (∑ i : I, D t (e i) * b i t ω) = D t (v t ω)
    have hrepr : (∑ i : I, b i t ω • e i) = v t ω := by
      simpa only [v, e, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr] using e.sum_repr (v t ω)
    rw [← hrepr, map_sum]
    simp only [map_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
  · have hi (j : J) (i k : I) :
        Integrable (fun t => H t (e i) (e k) *
          ((η i j).process t ω * (η k j).process t ω)) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) :=
      integrable_continuousOn_mul
        ((hH.clm_apply continuousOn_const).clm_apply continuousOn_const) (hProduct i k j)
    have hj (j : J) : Integrable (fun t => H t (σ j t ω) (σ j t ω))
        (TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
      refine (integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ =>
        integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun k _ => hi j i k))).congr
        (Eventually.of_forall fun t => ?_)
      change (∑ i : I, ∑ k : I, H t (e i) (e k) *
        ((η i j).process t ω * (η k j).process t ω)) = H t (σ j t ω) (σ j t ω)
      rw [euclidean_bilinear_eq_sum_basis]
      simp only [e, σ, mul_comm]
    exact (integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ => hj j)).const_mul _

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoGeneratorIntegrability

steps.title: Control coordinate products
steps.text: Cauchy–Schwarz on the sample-time product gives integrability of each product of two entries in the same noise column. Fubini gives integrability of the time sections.
steps.lean:
have hProducts : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ i k : I, ∀ j : J,
      Integrable (fun t => (η i j).process t ω * (η k j).process t ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) :=
    ae_all_iff.2 fun i => ae_all_iff.2 fun k => ae_all_iff.2 fun j =>
      ((η i j).memLp.integrable_mul (η k j).memLp).prod_right_ae
  filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 hbi, hX, hRange, hProducts] with ω hDrift hPath hK hProduct

steps.title: Control the derivative weights
steps.text: Along each selected continuous path, each evaluation of the first or second derivative on basis vectors is continuous and bounded on the compact horizon.
steps.lean:
have hm : MapsTo (fun t => X t ω) (Icc 0 T) K := fun _ ht => hK _ ht.2
  have hD : ContinuousOn D (Icc 0 T) :=
    (show ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ f) K from fun w hw =>
      ((hf w hw).continuousAt_fderiv (by decide)).continuousWithinAt).comp hPath hm
  have hH : ContinuousOn H (Icc 0 T) :=
    (show ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f)) K from fun w hw =>
      (((hf w hw).fderiv_right (m := 1) (by decide)).continuousAt_fderiv
        (by decide)).continuousWithinAt).comp hPath hm
steps.detail: Use the derivative continuity supplied by ContDiffAt and compactness of Icc.

steps.title: Sum over coordinates
steps.text: Expand the linear and bilinear forms in the finite Euclidean basis. Every summand is integrable, and the scalar factor one half preserves integrability.
steps.lean:
have hj (j : J) : Integrable (fun t => H t (σ j t ω) (σ j t ω))
        (TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
      refine (integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ =>
        integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun k _ => hi j i k))).congr
        (Eventually.of_forall fun t => ?_)
      change (∑ i : I, ∑ k : I, H t (e i) (e k) *
        ((η i j).process t ω * (η k j).process t ω)) = H t (σ j t ω) (σ j t ω)
      rw [euclidean_bilinear_eq_sum_basis]
      simp only [e, σ, mul_comm]
    exact (integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ => hj j)).const_mul _
steps.detail: Use the Euclidean coordinate expansions and integrable_finsetSum.
